sources.citation: Wolgemuth, Carl. 2007 [2002]. Nahuatl grammar of the townships of Mecayapan and Tatahuicapan de Juárez, Veracruz (English adaptation by Christopher S. Mackay of Gramática náhuatl (melaʼtájtol), 2nd ed., ILV 2002). 169 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the sister variety MECAYAPAN (nhx, isth1242), not nhk. §1.4 Accentuation, pp. 17-19: 'Words of two syllable or more are assumed to be accented on the second syllable from the end.. If the accent falls on a different syllable, this one is marked out with an acute accent (´). Monosyllables are not normally written with an accent.' Lists words accented on the last syllable (awél, ihkí:n, ihkó:n, nikpiá, nikpiáh; contractions kitéʔ, kimáʔ), interrogative vs relative pairs distinguished by accent (ka:n/ká:n), and antepenult accent only in words bearing enclitics (nikítaʔya).

en.wikipedia gives only the Mecayapan (nhx) orthographic convention (penultimate stress unmarked; acute marks other positions) and cites Ethnologue 16: Cosoleacaque 84% intelligible with Pajapan, 83% with Mecayapan. No nhk-specific source in either bibliography.

sources.citation: Ethnologue (SIL), 'Nahuatl, Isthmus-Cosoleacaque' (nhk), the Internet Archive 2023-03-09; OLAC 'resources in and about the Isthmus-Cosoleacaque Nahuatl language', the Internet Archive 2025-05-24
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. OLAC lists no archived resources for nhk beyond Glottolog/Ethnologue/LinguistList entries (no AILLA/ELAR deposit).

sources.citation: Peralta Ramírez, Valentín. 2005. El nawat de la costa del Golfo: algunas semejanzas y diferencias estructurales con el náhuatl central. CILLA II, University of Texas at Austin. 34 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress ('acento' absent). Describes Pajapan (nhp); §1.3.1 places Pajapan in an Isthmus group 'junto con el nawat de Mecayapan, Tatahuicapan y Zaragoza'.

sources.citation: García de León Griego, Antonio. 1969. Pajapan. Una variante del nahua del Este. Tesis de Licenciatura (Lingüística), ENAH, México. 184 pp. Part I (thesis pp. 20-45): glottochronology of 'nahua del Golfo' from 450-word lists collected in 1966 in 19 communities incl. Cosoleacaque, Coacotla, Oteapan, Zaragoza, Jáltipan, Soconusco (varieties COS, ZAR, JAL)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement for the Cosoleacaque/Zaragoza-Oteapan/Jáltipan varieties: Part I gives only comparative wordlists (occasional accent marks on COS forms) and the grouping (thesis p. 21): 'Los Tuxtlas y Pajapan son casi idénticas, y estas a Jáltipan-Soconusco; otra variante es la del municipio de Mecayapan que se liga bastante con la de Oteapan-Zaragoza. Cosoleacaque es casi idéntico a Ixhuatlán-Moloacán, a Tecominoacán y seguramente a San Felipe Río Nuevo'. The phonology chapter (thesis p. 51, §1.8: 'El acento recae por lo general en la penúltima sílaba.. fonémico.. aya/ayá, ga:wa/gawáh')…

sources.citation: García de León, Antonio. 1968. El dueño del maíz y otros relatos nahuas del sur de Veracruz. Tlalocan 5(4): 349-357 (texts from Zaragoza and Jáltipan).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only phoneme inventories of Zaragoza and Jáltipan (nhk-area localities); nothing on stress; texts unaccented.

sources.citation: Covarrubias, Miguel. 1946. Mexico South: The Isthmus of Tehuantepec. New York: Knopf. Appendix 'One hundred twenty words in seven Indian languages', col. NAHUAT (Cosoleacaque).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No rule; a 120-word Cosoleacaque Nahuat list with accents marked in the 1939 Americanist system (scanned degraded), plus ethnographic notes ('In Cosoleacaque the men speak fluent Spanish, but the women generally speak only Nahua').
